Using seconds instead of milliseconds in the CSS.
Running lighthouse on a cached page instead of a fresh load.

steps.do: Inspect the current foreground and background hex values in the Tailwind config.
Calculate the contrast ratio using a standard tool or online calculator.
Update the text utility to a shade that meets the 4.5:1 ratio, such as text-gray-900 on white.
Run a headless accessibility scan to verify the ratio.

traps: Assuming text-gray-600 is always compliant without checking the specific background color.
Forgetting that dark mode requires different shades to maintain the same contrast ratio.
Using arbitrary values like text-[#333] instead of standard Tailwind scales which are easier to verify.

steps.do: Install the virtualizer package.
In DataTable.vue, create a scroll container ref and call useVirtualizer with count rows.length, estimateSize 36, and overscan 8.
Give the scroll container a fixed height of 540px and render only virtualizer.getVirtualItems() rows inside tbody with transform translateY.

Using the array index as :key causes DOM churn while scrolling.

steps.do: Find the v-for over rows in the table body.
Add v-memo to the tr with dependencies row.version and whether row.id equals selectedId.
Keep :key on the same tr element, set to row.id.
Lint the component to catch template errors.
Time a single row selection on a 1000-row table, which must finish in under 200ms.

K-015553.example: The tr uses v-memo="[row.version, row.id === selectedId]" so selecting one row re-renders 2 rows out of 1000. The timing test asserts the update finishes in under 200ms.
K-015553.check: The test output shows the update time under 200ms and the re-rendered row count equals 2.
traps: Leaving a dependency out of v-memo leaves stale cell text on screen.
v-memo belongs on the same element as v-for, not on a wrapper.
v-memo does not replace :key, so keep both.

steps.do: Find where the row array is declared in the table component.
Replace ref(rows) with shallowRef(rows) and update rows.value only by assigning a new array.
Run the type checker to confirm the new ref type is accepted.
Time loading 50000 rows into the table, which must finish in under 500ms.

K-015554.example: const rows = shallowRef<Row[]>([]) then rows.value = await fetchRows() loads 50000 rows, and the test asserts the load takes under 500ms.
K-015554.check: The test prints the load time and it is under 500ms.
traps: With shallowRef, changing rows.value[0].name does not update the screen; assign a new array or new row object.
Do not use shallowRef if cells are edited in place and the array is never reassigned.
shallowRef still needs .value in script code.

steps.do: Search the components for v-for keys to find index-based keys.
Change each row :key to row.id, a unique value from the data.
Run the row identity test that sorts 10000 rows and counts recreated DOM nodes.
Run the unit tests for the table component.

K-015555.example: Sorting 10000 rows by name with :key="row.id" keeps the same 10000 tr nodes, and the identity test logs 0 nodes recreated.
K-015555.check: The identity test prints '0 nodes recreated' and the unit tests pass.
traps: Index keys make Vue reuse the wrong DOM nodes after a sort.
Duplicate ids cause a 'Duplicate keys' warning in development.
The key belongs on the tr inside v-for, not on a wrapper element.

steps.do: Find inline sort calls in the table component.
Move the sort and filter logic into a computed named visibleRows that copies the array before sorting.
Install the VueUse package to get a debounce helper.
Debounce the filter input by 150ms using useDebounceFn from @vueuse/core.
Time filter handling on 10000 rows, which must stay under 100ms per keystroke.

K-015556.example: Typing 'ann' into the search box on 10000 rows runs visibleRows once after a 150ms debounce, and the latency test reports 45ms. The computed uses [...rows.value].sort so the source array is not changed.
K-015556.check: The latency test prints a time under 100ms.
traps: Sorting inside the template reruns on every render.
Calling sort on rows.value directly mutates the source array; copy it first.
A debounce above 300ms makes the filter feel unresponsive.

steps.do: Find the column definitions and cell components in the table.
Wrap each cell component in the column definition with markRaw so Vue skips proxying it.
Load heavy cell renderers with defineAsyncComponent and a loading fallback.
Build for production and check the table chunk size, which must stay under 250kB gzip.
Run Lighthouse against the served production build of the table page and require a performance score of at least 90.

K-015557.example: const columns = shallowRef([{ key: 'name', cell: markRaw(NameCell) }]) keeps the cell component out of Vue's proxy system, and the Lighthouse run reports a performance score of 93.
K-015557.check: Lighthouse reports a performance score of 90 or higher and the build output shows the table chunk under 250kB gzip.
traps: Wrapping the whole rows array in markRaw breaks reactivity for the data.
Async cell components need a loading fallback or the cell renders blank.
Lighthouse must run against a built and served page, not the dev server.

steps.do: Install the motion package into the project.
Create the file src/components/tabs/Tabs.tsx and import motion from 'motion/react' at the top.

steps.do: Create the folder src/components/tabs for the tab component files.
Create src/components/tabs/Tabs.module.css with a .panel class that animates opacity from 0 to 1 and translateY from 4px to 0 over 200ms ease-out.
Add an @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that sets .panel animation to none.

Animating height or top with a transition causes layout work on every frame. Animate only opacity and transform.

steps.do: Install motion and vitest as dependencies for the build and test steps.
Install vitest as a dev dependency for testing the exit timing.
Wrap the panel in AnimatePresence with mode 'wait' and key the motion.div on the active tab id.
Set the exit transition to duration 0.15 and the enter transition to duration 0.15 in Tabs.tsx.
Write src/components/tabs/Tabs.test.tsx that clicks a second tab and asserts the first panel is removed from the DOM.
Run the test file to confirm the exit happens before the new panel appears.

K-015572.example: AnimatePresence mode='wait' wraps a motion.div with key='settings' so the 'profile' panel exits over 150ms before 'settings' enters. The exit and enter durations are both 0.15 seconds, which is 150ms each.
K-015572.check: npx vitest run src/components/tabs/Tabs.test.tsx prints '1 passed' or more with 0 failed, and the test sees only one tabpanel in the DOM after the animation.

steps.do: Open src/components/tabs/Tabs.tsx and import useReducedMotion from 'motion/react' alongside motion.
Call const reduce = useReducedMotion() at the top of the Tabs component.

Count the uses of useReducedMotion in the component file to confirm it is imported and called.
